name: Christian Religious Studies
topics: Creation and the fall of man
The patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph
Moses, the Exodus and the covenant
Leadership in Israel: Joshua and the judges
Prophets: Elijah, Elisha, Amos, Hosea, Isaiah and Jeremiah
Exile and return: Daniel, Ezra and Nehemiah
Birth, baptism, temptation and call of the disciples
Sermon on the Mount and other teachings
Trials, death and resurrection of Jesus
The early church: Pentecost, Peter, Stephen and Philip
Christian living: faith, love, works and civic duty

questions.q: According to the creation account in Genesis, on which day did God make the sun, moon and stars?
questions.e: Genesis 1:14-19 says God made the sun, moon and stars on the fourth day to rule the day and night. This was after He had already made light and separated the waters.
questions.p: Genesis 1:14-19 talk say na on the fourth day God create sun, moon and stars make dem rule day and night. E don already create light before then.

questions.q: In the Genesis account, what did God use to form the first man, Adam?
o: Water from the river in Eden
questions.e: Genesis 2:7 states that God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into him the breath of life, making him a living being.
questions.p: Genesis 2:7 talk say God mold man from dust of ground, then e blow breath of life enter am make man become living person.

questions.q: What did God do on the seventh day after completing the work of creation?
o: He rested from all His work
He formed Eve from Adam's rib
He planted the garden of Eden
questions.e: Genesis 2:2-3 records that God rested on the seventh day from all the work He had done, and He blessed and sanctified that day.
questions.p: Genesis 2:2-3 show say God rest on the seventh day comot from all the work wey e do, and e bless and set that day apart.

questions.q: From which part of Adam's body did God form Eve, according to Genesis?
questions.e: Genesis 2:21-22 tells how God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep, took one of his ribs, and made it into a woman, Eve.
questions.p: Genesis 2:21-22 explain say God make Adam sleep well well, comot one rib from am, then use the rib form woman wey be Eve.

questions.q: What name did God give to the tree whose fruit He forbade Adam and Eve to eat in the garden?
o: Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil
questions.e: Genesis 2:16-17 shows that God allowed Adam to eat from every tree except the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, warning he would die if he ate from it.
questions.p: Genesis 2:16-17 show say God allow Adam chop from every tree, but e warn am make e no touch Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, if not e go die.

questions.q: Immediately after Adam and Eve ate the forbidden fruit, what did they do out of shame before God confronted them?
o: They confessed their sin openly to God
They sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves
They ran away from the garden completely
They built an altar to offer sacrifice
questions.e: Genesis 3:7 says that as soon as their eyes were opened, Adam and Eve realised they were naked and sewed fig leaves together to make coverings for themselves.
questions.p: Genesis 3:7 talk say as their eye open, Adam and Eve realise say dem naked, so dem sew fig leaves together cover demselves.

questions.q: Which river is named in Genesis as one of the four rivers that branched out from the river flowing through the garden of Eden?
questions.e: Genesis 2:10-14 lists Pishon, Gihon, Hiddekel (Tigris) and Euphrates as the four rivers from Eden. Among the options, only the Euphrates matches this biblical list.
questions.p: Genesis 2:10-14 list Pishon, Gihon, Hiddekel (Tigris) and Euphrates as the four rivers wey comot for Eden. Na only Euphrates dey the options wey match this list.

questions.q: Before God changed his name as a sign of the covenant, what was Abraham originally called?
questions.e: God changed his name from Abram to Abraham to show he would be the father of many nations. This is recorded in Genesis 17:5.
questions.p: God change im name from Abram to Abraham because e go be papa of plenty nations. Na Genesis 17:5 talk am.

questions.q: After wrestling all night with a man at Peniel, Jacob received a new name. What was that name?
questions.e: The man told Jacob he would now be called Israel because he had struggled with God and with men and had prevailed. This is in Genesis 32:28.
questions.p: The man tell Jacob say im go now dey call Israel because e don fight with God and with men and e win. Na Genesis 32:28 talk am.

questions.q: When Joseph was taken to Egypt as a slave, which Egyptian official bought him?
questions.e: Joseph was sold to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, as recorded in Genesis 37:36.
questions.p: Dem sell Joseph give Potiphar, wey be Pharaoh officer and captain of guard. Na Genesis 37:36 talk am.

questions.q: God gave Abraham a sign to mark His covenant with him and his descendants. What was this sign?
questions.e: God commanded that every male among Abraham's household be circumcised as the everlasting sign of the covenant, as stated in Genesis 17:10-11. This distinguished Abraham's descendants as God's covenant people.
questions.p: God tell Abraham make dem circumcise every male for im house as sign of di covenant, na Genesis 17:10-11 talk am. Na so e take mark Abraham pikin dem as God covenant people.

questions.q: At which place did Jacob see in a dream a ladder reaching to heaven with angels going up and down on it?
questions.e: Jacob had this dream while fleeing from Esau and resting at a place he later named Bethel, meaning 'house of God'. The account is in Genesis 28:10-19.
questions.p: Jacob see dis dream as e dey run comot from Esau, e rest for one place wey e later call Bethel, meaning 'house of God'. Na Genesis 28:10-19 talk am.

questions.q: Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dream of seven fat cows followed by seven thin cows to mean that:
o: seven years of famine would come before seven years of plenty
seven years of war would be followed by seven years of peace
seven kings would rule Egypt in turn
seven years of plenty would be followed by seven years of famine
questions.e: Joseph explained that Egypt would first enjoy seven years of abundant harvest, then suffer seven years of severe famine, so Pharaoh should store grain during the good years. This interpretation is found in Genesis 41:29-30.
questions.p: Joseph explain say Egypt go first enjoy seven years wey plenty food dey, then seven years of hunger go follow, so make Pharaoh store grain during di good years. Na Genesis 41:29-30 talk am.

questions.q: How many sons did Jacob have who became the ancestors of the twelve tribes of Israel?
questions.e: Jacob had twelve sons through his wives Leah and Rachel and their maidservants, and these became the twelve tribes of Israel. The list is given in Genesis 35:22-26.
questions.p: Jacob get sons twelve through im wives Leah and Rachel and dia maidservants, and dis ones become di twelve tribes of Israel. Na Genesis 35:22-26 give di list.

questions.q: As a baby, Moses was placed in a basket made of papyrus reeds and set among the reeds along a river bank to save him from Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew baby boys. Who found and adopted him?
questions.e: Pharaoh's daughter came to bathe at the river, saw the basket, and took Moses as her own son. This is recorded in Exodus 2:5-10.
questions.p: Na Pharaoh daughter come bath for river, she see the basket wey carry Moses and she pick am as her own pikin. Dis story dey for Exodus 2:5-10.

questions.q: While keeping the flock of his father-in-law Jethro near Horeb, Moses saw a bush that was burning but not consumed by the fire. What did God instruct Moses to do before approaching?
o: Remove his sandals because the ground was holy
questions.e: God told Moses to remove his sandals because he was standing on holy ground. This encounter is found in Exodus 3:5.
questions.p: God tell Moses make e comot im sandals because the ground na holy ground. Na so e dey for Exodus 3:5.

questions.q: God sent a series of plagues on Egypt to compel Pharaoh to release the Israelites. Which of the following was the final and most severe plague that finally made Pharaoh let the people go?
questions.e: The tenth and final plague was the death of every firstborn in Egypt, which broke Pharaoh's resistance. This is recorded in Exodus 12:29-32.
questions.p: Di tenth and last plague na death of all firstborn for Egypt, and na dat one make Pharaoh release di Israelites. E dey for Exodus 12:29-32.

questions.q: During the first Passover in Egypt, the Israelites were instructed to apply blood on their doorposts. What was the purpose of this blood marking?
o: To signal the time for departure
To identify Hebrew houses for tax collection
To show which houses needed food supplies
To cause the death angel to pass over their homes without killing their firstborn
questions.e: The blood on the doorposts was a sign so that the destroying angel would pass over the houses of the Israelites and spare their firstborn. This is found in Exodus 12:13.
questions.p: Di blood wey dem put for doorpost na sign make di angel of death pass over dia house and no kill dia firstborn. E dey for Exodus 12:13.

questions.q: After leading the Israelites out of Egypt, Moses went up a mountain where God gave him the Ten Commandments written on tablets of stone. What is the name of this mountain?
questions.e: God gave Moses the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai, as recorded in Exodus 19 and 20.
questions.p: Na for Mount Sinai God give Moses di Ten Commandments, and e dey for Exodus 19 and 20.

questions.q: When the Israelites reached the Red Sea with Pharaoh's army pursuing them, God instructed Moses to stretch out his hand over the sea. What immediately happened as a result?
o: The sea was divided, making a dry path for the people to cross
The sea became calm for swimming
A storm destroyed Pharaoh's chariots instantly
questions.e: When Moses stretched his hand over the sea, God drove the water back with a strong wind, dividing the sea so the Israelites could cross on dry ground. This is in Exodus 14:21.
questions.p: Wen Moses stretch im hand ova di sea, God use strong wind divide di sea so dat di Israelites fit cross for dry ground. E dey for Exodus 14:21.

questions.q: While Moses was on the mountain receiving God's instructions for a long period, the Israelites grew impatient and asked Aaron to make them a god they could see. What did Aaron make for them?
questions.e: Aaron collected gold earrings from the people and molded them into a golden calf, which the Israelites worshipped. This act of idolatry is recorded in Exodus 32:1-4.
questions.p: Aaron collect gold earrings from di pipo and melt am make golden calf, wey di Israelites begin worship. Dis idolatry story dey for Exodus 32:1-4.

questions.q: At Mount Sinai, God established a covenant with Israel through Moses, promising to make them His special people if they obeyed His laws. Based on the terms of this covenant, what was Israel's primary responsibility in return for God's protection and blessing?
o: To build a permanent temple immediately
To obey God's commandments and keep His statutes
questions.e: The covenant at Sinai required Israel to keep God's commandments and statutes in order to remain His chosen people and receive His blessings. This conditional agreement is stated in Exodus 19:5-6.
questions.p: Di covenant for Sinai tell Israel say dem must obey God commandments and statutes make dem remain im chosen pipo and receive im blessings. Dis agreement dey for Exodus 19:5-6.

questions.q: After the death of Moses, who did God appoint to lead the Israelites into the Promised Land of Canaan?
questions.e: God spoke to Joshua, the son of Nun and former assistant of Moses, and told him to lead Israel across the Jordan into Canaan. This is recorded in Joshua 1:1-2.
questions.p: Na Joshua, wey be Moses im assistant, God talk make e lead Israel enter Canaan after Moses don die. Dis dey for Joshua 1:1-2.

questions.q: Before Israel crossed the River Jordan, Joshua sent two spies to gather information about which city, where they were hidden by a woman named Rahab?
questions.e: Joshua sent two men to secretly view the land, especially Jericho, and they stayed in the house of Rahab the harlot who hid them from the king's men. This is found in Joshua 2:1.
questions.p: Joshua send two spy go check Jericho land, and Rahab hide dem for her house when the king people come find dem. Dis story dey for Joshua 2:1.

questions.q: How did the strong walls of Jericho finally fall before the Israelites, according to the Bible account?
o: The priests blew trumpets and the people shouted after marching round the city for seven days
The Israelites dug a tunnel under the wall
An earthquake destroyed the walls at night
The Israelites broke it down with battering rams
questions.e: God instructed Joshua that the people should march round Jericho once daily for six days, and seven times on the seventh day; when the priests blew the trumpets and the people shouted, the wall collapsed. This miracle is in Joshua 6:1-20.
questions.p: God tell Joshua make dem waka round Jericho one time every day for six days, then seven times on di seventh day; when priest blow trumpet and people shout, di wall fall flat. Dis miracle dey for Joshua 6:1-20.

questions.q: What made Deborah's role among the judges of Israel especially unique compared to Gideon and Samson?
o: She was the only judge who built a temple for worship
She was a priest who offered sacrifices in the tabernacle
She was a prophetess and judge who directed Barak to defeat Sisera's army
She was a foreign princess who married an Israelite king
questions.e: Deborah was both a prophetess and a judge, and she gave military instructions to Barak which led to Israel's victory over Sisera, the Canaanite commander. This account is in Judges 4:4-16.
questions.p: Deborah na prophetess and judge, and she instruct Barak on how to fight and defeat Sisera, di Canaanite army commander. Dis story dey for Judges 4:4-16.

questions.q: In the story of Deborah and Barak, who actually killed Sisera, the fleeing Canaanite army commander, after he sought refuge in her tent?
questions.e: Sisera fled to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, who gave him milk to drink and then drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept. This is recorded in Judges 4:17-21.
questions.p: Sisera run go hide for Jael tent, wey be Heber im wife, and Jael give am milk drink before she use tent peg knock am for head as e sleep. Dis dey for Judges 4:17-21.

questions.q: Before leading Israel against the Midianites, Gideon tested God's call on him twice using a fleece of wool placed on the threshing floor overnight. What was the sign he asked for and received?
o: Fire falling from heaven to burn the fleece
Rain falling for seven days without stopping
A voice speaking audibly from the fleece
Dew forming only on the fleece while the ground stayed dry, then the reverse the next night
questions.e: Gideon asked God to make dew appear only on the fleece while the ground remained dry, and then reversed the test, asking for dew on the ground but a dry fleece; both happened, confirming his call. This is found in Judges 6:36-40.
questions.p: Gideon ask God make dew wet only di fleece while ground remain dry, then e reverse am make ground wet while fleece dry; both tin happen as God confirm im call. Dis dey for Judges 6:36-40.

questions.q: Who was the mother of Samuel, who dedicated her son to serve God at the tabernacle in Shiloh after he was weaned?
questions.e: Hannah prayed for a son and promised to give him to God's service. When Samuel was born, she kept her vow and took him to Shiloh. This is recorded in 1 Samuel 1:20-28.
questions.p: Na Hannah pray God make im get pikin, im promise say im go give the pikin to God service. When Samuel born, Hannah carry am go Shiloh as im promise. Dis dey for 1 Samuel 1:20-28.

questions.q: Under whose care did the young Samuel grow up and serve while ministering at the tabernacle in Shiloh?
questions.e: Hannah left Samuel with Eli the priest at Shiloh, where the boy grew up serving before the Lord. God later called Samuel while he was under Eli's care. See 1 Samuel 3:1.
questions.p: Hannah leave Samuel with Eli the priest for Shiloh, na so the boy dey grow dey serve God. Na there God call Samuel first time. E dey for 1 Samuel 3:1.

questions.q: According to 1 Samuel chapter 15, what exact disobedience caused God to reject Saul as king of Israel?
o: He failed to completely destroy the Amalekites and their livestock as commanded
He built an altar to a foreign god on Mount Carmel
He married a woman from a forbidden nation
He refused to go to war against the Philistines
questions.e: God commanded Saul to destroy the Amalekites and all their animals completely, but Saul spared King Agag and the best animals. Samuel told him that obedience is better than sacrifice. This is in 1 Samuel 15:3, 9, 22-23.
questions.p: God tell Saul make im destroy all Amalekite people and their animals finish, but Saul leave King Agag and the best animals. Samuel talk say to obey pass sacrifice. E dey for 1 Samuel 15:3, 9, 22-23.

questions.q: Who anointed David as king over Israel while his brothers stood watching at Jesse's house in Bethlehem?
questions.e: God sent Samuel to Jesse's house to anoint one of his sons as king. After rejecting the older sons, Samuel anointed David, the youngest, as the Spirit of the Lord came upon him. This is in 1 Samuel 16:1-13.
questions.p: God send Samuel go Jesse house make im anoint one of im sons as king. Afta e reject the big brothers, Samuel anoint David wey be the last born, and Spirit of God come enter am. E dey for 1 Samuel 16:1-13.

questions.q: What weapon did David use to defeat the Philistine giant Goliath on the battlefield at the Valley of Elah?
o: A sling and a smooth stone
questions.e: David refused Saul's armour and instead chose five smooth stones and his sling, striking Goliath on the forehead with one stone. He then used Goliath's own sword to kill him. This is recorded in 1 Samuel 17:40, 49-50.
questions.p: David no gree wear Saul armour, im pick five smooth stones with im sling, im hit Goliath for forehead with one stone. Na Goliath im sword im later use finish am. E dey for 1 Samuel 17:40, 49-50.

questions.q: Why did King Saul become jealous and afraid of David after his victory over Goliath and the Philistines?
o: David married Saul's daughter without asking permission
David refused to serve as a soldier in Saul's army
The women of Israel sang that David had killed tens of thousands while Saul had killed only thousands
Saul's own son Jonathan crowned David king in public
questions.e: When the army returned from battle, women sang that Saul had slain thousands but David had slain ten thousands. This song made Saul jealous and suspicious of David from that day. See 1 Samuel 18:6-9.
questions.p: When soldiers dey comot from war, women sing say Saul kill thousand but David kill ten thousand. Dis song make Saul jealous and im begin suspect David from that day. E dey for 1 Samuel 18:6-9.

questions.q: When Samuel looked at Jesse's eldest son Eliab and was impressed by his height and appearance, what lesson did God teach him before David was chosen as king?
o: That God looks at the heart, not outward appearance, when choosing a leader
That physical strength is the most important quality for a king
That the first son of any family always inherits leadership
That God chooses leaders mainly by their outward appearance and height
questions.e: Samuel assumed Eliab's impressive looks meant he was God's choice, but God told him not to judge by outward appearance because man looks at the outside while God looks at the heart. This teaching came just before David was anointed. See 1 Samuel 16:6-7.
questions.p: Samuel think say Eliab fine body mean say na im be the choice, but God tell am make im no judge by outside appearance because man dey see outside, God dey see inside heart. Na so e be before David anointing. E dey for 1 Samuel 16:6-7.

questions.q: Who was Saul's father, a man of standing from the tribe of Benjamin, as recorded in 1 Samuel?
questions.e: Saul was the son of Kish, a wealthy and respected man of the tribe of Benjamin. Saul was sent to search for his father's lost donkeys when he first met Samuel. This is in 1 Samuel 9:1-3.
questions.p: Saul na son of Kish, wey be rich and respected man from Benjamin tribe. Na when Saul dey find im papa donkeys wey lost, e first meet Samuel. E dey for 1 Samuel 9:1-3.

questions.q: At Gibeon, God appeared to Solomon in a dream and asked him to request anything he wanted. What did Solomon ask for?
o: An understanding heart to judge the people well
A large kingdom bigger than his father's
questions.e: Solomon asked God for an understanding heart to judge the people and to tell good from evil, instead of asking for riches or long life. God was pleased and gave him wisdom plus riches and honour. This is recorded in 1 Kings 3:5-9.
questions.p: Solomon no ask for money or long life, na wisdom heart wey go help am judge im people well-well im ask for. God like am well and e give am wisdom plus riches sef. Na 1 Kings 3:5-9 talk am.

questions.q: How many years did King Solomon spend to complete the building of the temple in Jerusalem?
questions.e: The Bible records that Solomon started the temple in the fourth year of his reign and finished it in the eleventh year, making it seven years. This is found in 1 Kings 6:38.
questions.p: Solomon start the temple for im fourth year as king and finish am for eleventh year, so na seven years total. E dey written for 1 Kings 6:38.

questions.q: Which foreign ruler travelled to Jerusalem to test Solomon's wisdom with difficult questions and was amazed by his riches and wisdom?
questions.e: The Queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame and came with hard questions to test him, and she was greatly impressed by his wisdom and wealth. This story is told in 1 Kings 10:1-9.
questions.p: Queen of Sheba hear about Solomon reputation so e come test am with hard questions, and im wisdom and wealth shock am well-well. The story dey for 1 Kings 10:1-9.

questions.q: According to the Bible, what was the main reason God told Solomon that his kingdom would be taken away from his descendants?
o: He failed to complete the building of the temple
He oppressed the poor with heavy taxes
He refused to pay tribute to neighbouring kings
His foreign wives turned his heart to worship other gods
questions.e: Solomon's many foreign wives turned his heart away from the Lord to worship idols like Ashtoreth and Molech, which angered God. Because of this sin, God told him the kingdom would be torn away, though not in his own lifetime. This is in 1 Kings 11:4-11.
questions.p: Solomon plenty foreign wives turn im mind comot from God make e begin worship idols like Ashtoreth and Molech. Na dis sin make God vex and tell am say im kingdom go tear comot, but no be for im own time. Dis dey for 1 Kings 11:4-11.

questions.q: When the people asked Rehoboam to lighten the heavy labour his father Solomon had placed on them, whose advice did Rehoboam follow?
o: The young men who grew up with him
The elders who had served his father Solomon
questions.e: Rehoboam rejected the gentle advice of the older elders and instead followed the harsh advice of the young men he grew up with, promising even heavier burdens. This foolish decision led directly to the division of the kingdom, as recorded in 1 Kings 12:8-14.
questions.p: Rehoboam no listen to the old elders wey advise am make e gentle, instead e follow im age-mates wey tell am make e dey harsh pass im papa. Na dis foolish choice cause the kingdom to split, 1 Kings 12:8-14 talk am.

questions.q: After the kingdom split into two, which tribe, apart from Judah, remained loyal to Rehoboam in the southern kingdom?
questions.e: When the ten northern tribes followed Jeroboam, only the tribe of Benjamin remained with Judah under Rehoboam's rule, forming the southern kingdom. This grouping is confirmed in 1 Kings 12:21.
questions.p: When the ten northern tribes follow Jeroboam comot, na only Benjamin remain with Judah under Rehoboam for the southern kingdom. 1 Kings 12:21 confam dis one.

questions.q: Which prophet tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave ten pieces to Jeroboam as a sign that he would rule over ten tribes of Israel?
questions.e: The prophet Ahijah met Jeroboam on the road, tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten, symbolising that God would give Jeroboam ten tribes because of Solomon's idolatry. This event is recorded in 1 Kings 11:29-31.
questions.p: Prophet Ahijah meet Jeroboam for road, tear im new cloth into twelve pieces and give am ten, to show say God go give am ten tribes because of Solomon idol worship. Na 1 Kings 11:29-31 talk am.

questions.q: After becoming king over the ten northern tribes, what did Jeroboam do to stop the people from travelling to Jerusalem to worship?
o: He forbade the people from travelling south
He built a rival temple in Shechem
He appointed only Levites as his royal guards
He set up two golden calves at Bethel and Dan
questions.e: Jeroboam feared losing his people's loyalty if they kept worshipping in Jerusalem, so he made two golden calves and placed them at Bethel and Dan for the people to worship instead. This act of idolatry is recorded in 1 Kings 12:28-29.
questions.p: Jeroboam fear say if im people dey always go Jerusalem for worship, dem go return go Rehoboam, so e make two gold calves and put dem for Bethel and Dan make dem worship instead. Na idolatry wey dey written for 1 Kings 12:28-29.

questions.q: While Elijah hid by the brook Cherith during the famine, who brought him bread and meat morning and evening?
questions.e: God commanded ravens to feed Elijah with bread and meat by the brook Cherith. This showed God's care for His prophet even in a time of famine. See 1 Kings 17:4-6.
questions.p: God tell ravens make dem carry bread and meat come give Elijah for mor ning and evening wen e dey hide for Cherith. Na so God take show say E dey care for im prophet even for hungry time. Check 1 Kings 17:4-6.

questions.q: Before Elijah was taken up to heaven, what did Elisha specifically ask him for?
questions.e: Elisha asked Elijah for a double portion of his spirit so that he could continue the prophetic work powerfully. Elijah told him this was a hard request but granted it. See 2 Kings 2:9-10.
questions.p: Elisha beg Elijah make e give am double portion of im spirit so e fit continue the prophet work well well. Elijah tell am say na hard thing but e still grant am. Check 2 Kings 2:9-10.

questions.q: Naaman, the Syrian army commander, was healed of leprosy after dipping himself seven times in which river, as Elisha instructed?
questions.e: Elisha told Naaman to wash seven times in the River Jordan, and his skin became clean like a young boy's. This miracle showed the power of God working through Elisha's word. See 2 Kings 5:10-14.
questions.p: Elisha tell Naaman make e go wash imsef seven times for River Jordan, and im skin come clean like small pikin own. Na so God power take show through Elisha word. Check 2 Kings 5:10-14.

questions.q: When Amaziah the priest told Amos to stop prophesying and go back home, how did Amos describe his original occupation before God called him?
o: A herdsman and dresser of sycamore trees
questions.e: Amos told Amaziah that he was not a trained prophet by profession but a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore trees whom God took and sent to prophesy. This shows God can call ordinary people for His work. See Amos 7:14-15.
questions.p: Amos tell Amaziah say im no be prophet by training, na herdsman and sycamore tree dresser wey God carry send message. Dis one show say God fit use ordinary person for im work. Check Amos 7:14-15.

questions.q: God commanded Hosea to marry Gomer, a woman given to unfaithfulness. What did this marriage symbolize about Israel?
o: The importance of forgiveness among couples
questions.e: Hosea's marriage to Gomer was a living picture of Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness to God through idol worship, while God still loved and wanted to restore them. See Hosea 1:2-3.
questions.p: Hosea marriage to Gomer na picture wey show how Israel no faithful to God because dem dey worship idol, but God still love dem and wan bring dem back. Check Hosea 1:2-3.

questions.q: In Isaiah's vision of God's glory in the temple, what did a seraphim use to touch his lips to take away his guilt?
o: A live coal taken with tongs from the altar
questions.e: A seraphim flew to Isaiah with a live coal taken with tongs from the altar and touched his lips, declaring his guilt removed and sin atoned for. This prepared him to accept God's call. See Isaiah 6:6-7.
questions.p: One seraphim carry live coal wey e use tongs take from altar come touch Isaiah mouth, e talk say im guilt don comot and sin don clear. Dis one make am ready to answer God call. Check Isaiah 6:6-7.

questions.q: When God called Jeremiah to be a prophet to the nations, what excuse did Jeremiah initially give for not wanting to accept the task?
questions.e: Jeremiah told God he did not know how to speak because he was only a youth, but God assured him He would be with him and put words in his mouth. See Jeremiah 1:6-9.
questions.p: Jeremiah tell God say e no sabi how to talk because e still young, but God tell am say E go dey with am and go put word for im mouth. Check Jeremiah 1:6-9.

questions.q: Which prophet called down fire from heaven to consume two groups of fifty soldiers sent by King Ahaziah to arrest him?
questions.e: King Ahaziah sent soldiers to arrest Elijah, but Elijah called fire down from heaven that consumed them, showing God's protection over His prophet. See 2 Kings 1:9-12.
questions.p: King Ahaziah send soja come arrest Elijah, but Elijah call fire from heaven wey burn dem finish. Na so God take protect im prophet. Check 2 Kings 1:9-12.

questions.q: In the book of Daniel, what new Babylonian name did the chief official give to Daniel when he was brought into King Nebuchadnezzar's palace?
questions.e: The chief official renamed Daniel 'Belteshazzar', while his three friends were renamed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. This is recorded in Daniel 1:7.
questions.p: Di oga for palace change Daniel name to 'Belteshazzar'. Im three friends na dem dem call Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. Daniel 1:7 talk am.

questions.q: Daniel and his three friends refused the king's rich food and wine, and asked instead to be given what kind of food to test God's provision?
questions.e: Daniel asked the guard to test them for ten days on vegetables and water instead of the king's food, and they looked healthier afterward. This is found in Daniel 1:12.
questions.p: Daniel beg di guard make dem try dem with vegetables and water for ten days instead of king chop. After di ten days, dem body shine pass di oda boys. Daniel 1:12 dey talk am.

questions.q: Daniel was thrown into a den of lions as punishment because he continued to do what, despite a royal decree forbidding it?
o: Praying three times a day to God
Refusing to bow to a golden image
questions.e: King Darius signed a decree that no one should pray to any god or man except him, but Daniel kept praying three times daily, so he was thrown into the lions' den. This is in Daniel 6:10-16.
questions.p: King Darius sign law say make nobody pray to any god except am, but Daniel still dey pray three times every day. Dat na why dem throw am inside lion den. Na Daniel 6:10-16 talk am.

questions.q: Who correctly interpreted King Nebuchadnezzar's dream about a large statue made of gold, silver, bronze, iron and clay?
questions.e: Daniel, with God's help, told the king his dream and explained that the statue's different materials represented a series of kingdoms. This account is in Daniel chapter 2.
questions.p: Daniel, wit God im help, explain di dream to Nebuchadnezzar say di different materials for di statue show different kingdoms wey go come. Na Daniel chapter 2 talk am.

questions.q: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were thrown into a blazing furnace because they refused to do what, according to the book of Daniel?
o: Bow down to the golden image Nebuchadnezzar set up
questions.e: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and ordered everyone to worship it, but the three young men refused, so they were thrown into the fiery furnace. This is recorded in Daniel 3:12-20.
questions.p: Nebuchadnezzar build gold image and tell everybody make dem worship am, but di three boys no gree. Na im dem throw dem enter di fire furnace. Daniel 3:12-20 dey talk am.

questions.q: Who was the priest and scribe who led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem and later taught the people the Law of Moses after the exile?
questions.e: Ezra was a priest and skilled scribe in the Law of Moses who led exiles back to Jerusalem and publicly read and taught the Law to the people. This is described in Ezra chapter 7 and Nehemiah chapter 8.
questions.p: Ezra na priest and scribe wey sabi di Law of Moses well well, im lead exiles go back Jerusalem and later teach di people di Law. Na Ezra 7 and Nehemiah 8 talk am.

questions.q: When Nehemiah received a report about Jerusalem while he was serving as cupbearer in Persia, what exactly did the report describe about the city?
o: The walls were broken down and the gates burned with fire
The temple had been rebuilt and dedicated
The king had ordered the city destroyed again
The people had returned to idol worship
questions.e: Nehemiah's brother Hanani told him that the survivors in Jerusalem were in trouble and disgrace, with the wall broken down and its gates burned, which made Nehemiah weep and pray. This is in Nehemiah 1:3-4.
questions.p: Hanani tell Nehemiah say di people wey remain for Jerusalem dey suffer shame because di wall don break and dem burn di gates. Na dat news make Nehemiah cry and pray. Nehemiah 1:3-4 talk am.

questions.q: While rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem, Nehemiah organized the workers so that half held tools and the other half held weapons. This arrangement was a direct response to opposition from which two men mentioned in the account?
questions.e: Sanballat and Tobiah mocked and plotted to attack the builders, so Nehemiah had half the workers hold weapons for defence while the rest worked, showing wisdom in facing opposition. This is recorded in Nehemiah 4:1-18.
questions.p: Sanballat and Tobiah dey mock and plan to attack di builders, so Nehemiah arrange am make half carry weapon protect dem while di oda half dey work. E show as im sabi handle wahala. Nehemiah 4:1-18 talk am.

questions.q: In the Gospel of Luke, which angel appeared to Mary to announce that she would give birth to Jesus?
questions.e: Luke 1:26-31 records that God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary in Nazareth to tell her she would conceive and give birth to Jesus.
questions.p: Luke 1:26-31 talk say na angel Gabriel God send go meet Mary for Nazareth to tell am say she go born Jesus.

questions.q: Who baptized Jesus in the River Jordan before he began his public ministry?
questions.e: Matthew 3:13-17 tells us that Jesus came to John the Baptist at the River Jordan to be baptized by him, though John first hesitated.
questions.p: Matthew 3:13-17 talk say Jesus go meet John the Baptist for River Jordan make e baptize am, even though John first hesitate.

questions.q: What sign came down upon Jesus immediately after his baptism, according to Matthew's Gospel?
questions.e: Matthew 3:16 states that after Jesus was baptized, the heavens opened and the Spirit of God descended like a dove and rested on him.
questions.p: Matthew 3:16 talk say after dem baptize Jesus, heaven open and Spirit of God come down like dove come land for him body.

questions.q: For how many days did Jesus fast in the wilderness before the devil came to tempt him?
questions.e: Matthew 4:2 says Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights in the wilderness, after which he became hungry and the devil came to tempt him.
questions.p: Matthew 4:2 talk say Jesus fast for forty days and forty night for wilderness before devil come tempt am when hunger catch am.

questions.q: When the devil challenged Jesus to turn stones into bread during the temptation in the wilderness, from which Old Testament book did Jesus quote his reply that 'man shall not live by bread alone'?
questions.e: In Matthew 4:4, Jesus answers the devil by quoting Deuteronomy 8:3, which teaches that man does not live by bread alone but by every word from God.
questions.p: Matthew 4:4 show say Jesus use word from Deuteronomy 8:3 reply devil say man no go only live by bread, but by every word wey come from God mouth.

questions.q: Which two brothers, who were fishermen, did Jesus first call by the Sea of Galilee to become his disciples?
questions.e: Matthew 4:18-20 records that Jesus saw Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew casting their net into the sea and called them to follow him.
questions.p: Matthew 4:18-20 talk say Jesus see Simon wey dem dey call Peter and im brother Andrew as dem dey throway net for sea, e come call dem make dem follow am.

questions.q: Matthew the tax collector was called by Jesus while he was at a particular place doing his job. Where was Matthew when Jesus called him to become a disciple?
questions.e: Matthew 9:9 narrates that Jesus saw Matthew sitting at the tax collector's booth collecting taxes and said to him, 'Follow me,' and Matthew got up and followed him.
questions.p: Matthew 9:9 talk say Jesus see Matthew as e dey sidon for im tax collection table, Jesus tell am 'Follow me,' Matthew come stand up follow am.

questions.q: At the pool called Bethesda in Jerusalem, Jesus healed a man who had suffered from his sickness for how many years before he was made whole?
questions.e: The man had been sick for thirty-eight years before Jesus healed him and told him to take up his bed and walk. This is recorded in John 5:5-9.
questions.p: Di man don dey sick for thirty-eight years before Jesus heal am and tell am make e carry im mat waka. Dis dey for John 5:5-9.

questions.q: When Jesus fed a large crowd near the Sea of Galilee with a boy's food items, the boy brought five loaves of bread and how many fish?
questions.e: A young boy provided five barley loaves and two small fish, which Jesus multiplied to feed over five thousand people. This miracle is found in John 6:9-13.
questions.p: One small boy bring five bread and two fish, na dis one Jesus multiply feed plenty people wey pass five thousand. Dis miracle dey for John 6:9-13.

questions.q: When Jesus was called to the house of a synagogue official whose daughter had just died, what did Jesus say about the girl's condition before He raised her back to life?
o: She has been dead too long
questions.e: Jesus said the girl was only sleeping, even though mourners laughed at Him, and then He raised her up by the hand. This miracle is recorded in Mark 5:39-42.
questions.p: Jesus talk say di girl dey sleep nothing more, even though people wey dey cry begin laugh am, den e raise am wit im hand. Dis dey for Mark 5:39-42.

questions.q: Which miracle of Jesus teaches that He could heal a sick person without being physically present at that person's location?
o: Healing of the woman with the issue of blood
questions.e: A Roman centurion in Capernaum asked Jesus to only 'say the word' and his servant would be healed, showing great faith, and Jesus healed the servant from a distance. This is in Matthew 8:5-13.
questions.p: One Roman centurion for Capernaum beg Jesus make e just 'talk word' make im servant better, e no need waka go house, Jesus bless am well well because of im faith. Dis dey for Matthew 8:5-13.

questions.q: What key lesson do Christians learn from the miracle where Jesus calmed the storm on the Sea of Galilee while His disciples panicked in the boat?
questions.e: Jesus rebuked the wind and said 'Peace, be still', and the sea became calm, showing His authority over nature. This event teaches believers to trust in His power, as recorded in Mark 4:35-41.
questions.p: Jesus talk give di wind and sea say 'Peace, quiet down', e kwa quiet, dis show say e get power over nature. Di lesson na make believers trust am, e dey for Mark 4:35-41.

questions.q: In John chapter 9, Jesus healed a man who had been blind from birth. When His disciples asked whether the man's own sin or his parents' sin caused the blindness, what reason did Jesus give instead?
o: His parents refused to worship God
That God's work might be displayed in his life
questions.e: Jesus rejected the idea that sin caused the blindness and said it happened so that the works of God could be revealed in the man's life. This teaching is found in John 9:1-3.
questions.p: Jesus no gree say na sin cause di blindness, e talk say na so dat God works go show for di man life. Dis teaching dey for John 9:1-3.

questions.q: Before Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead at Bethany, how many days had Lazarus already spent in the tomb?
questions.e: Martha told Jesus that Lazarus had been in the tomb four days and that his body would already be decaying, yet Jesus still raised him. This is recorded in John 11:39.
questions.p: Martha tell Jesus say Lazarus don dey tomb reach four days, im body don begin smell, but Jesus still raise am. Dis dey for John 11:39.

questions.q: Jesus performed His first recorded miracle, turning water into wine, at a wedding feast held in which town?
questions.e: Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding in Cana of Galilee after His mother told Him the wine had finished. This was His first miracle, recorded in John 2:1-11.
questions.p: Jesus turn water to wine for wedding wey dey Cana for Galilee, afta im mama tell am say wine don finish. Na im first miracle, e dey for John 2:1-11.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Sower, Jesus explained that the seed which fell among thorns represented those who hear the word but later fail to bear fruit. What exactly happened to that seed?
o: It withered because it had no root
The thorns grew up and choked it
questions.e: Jesus said the seed among thorns represents people who hear the word, but the worries of life and love of riches (the thorns) grow up and choke it so it yields no fruit. This is found in Matthew 13:7 and 13:22.
questions.p: Jesus talk say the seed wey fall for thorns na im be people wey hear word but worry and love of money choke the word so e no bear fruit. Dis dey Matthew 13:7 and 13:22.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, what did the younger son do immediately after his father gave him his share of the property?
o: He travelled to a far country and wasted it in reckless living
He invested it in his father's farmland
He gave it all to the poor in his village
He saved it for future use
questions.e: After collecting his portion, the younger son journeyed to a distant country where he squandered his wealth through wild and reckless living, which later led to his poverty. This is recorded in Luke 15:13.
questions.p: After the small son collect im share, e travel go far country go waste the money with bad life and enjoyment wey no make sense. Na dis one bring poverty come meet am, Luke 15:13 talk am.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, which two people passed by the wounded traveller on the road without helping him before the Samaritan arrived?
o: A tax collector and a scribe
questions.e: Jesus said a priest and then a Levite both saw the wounded man but passed by on the other side without helping him, before the Samaritan showed mercy. This teaching is found in Luke 10:31-33.
questions.p: Jesus talk say na priest first pass, then Levite follow pass, but the two of dem no help the injured man until the Samaritan come show am mercy. Dis one dey Luke 10:31-33.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep, how many sheep did the shepherd leave behind in the open field in order to go and search for the one sheep that had wandered away?
questions.e: The shepherd in the parable had a hundred sheep; when one went missing, he left the ninety-nine others to go and find the lost one, showing how much God values each soul. This is recorded in Luke 15:4.
questions.p: The shepherd get hundred sheep; when one miss, e leave the remaining ninety-nine go find the one wey lost, to show as God dey value every single soul. Na so e dey for Luke 15:4.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Talents, the master shared his wealth among three servants before travelling. How many talents did the servant who received the smallest amount get?
questions.e: The master gave five talents to one servant, two to another, and only one talent to the third, each according to his ability. This is found in Matthew 25:15.
questions.p: The master give one servant five talent, another one two talent, and the last one just one talent, according to as e fit carry am. Na so Matthew 25:15 talk am.

questions.q: A rich farmer in one of Jesus' parables planned to pull down his barns and build bigger ones to store his abundant harvest, but God called him a fool because he would die that same night. What key lesson does this parable mainly teach?
o: The need to build bigger barns for storage
The reward that comes from hard work
The importance of saving for the future
The danger of trusting in riches instead of God
questions.e: The Parable of the Rich Fool warns against storing up treasure for oneself while neglecting one's relationship with God, since life and material wealth can end suddenly. This is taught in Luke 12:16-21.
questions.p: The Parable of the Rich Fool dey warn people say make dem no dey store riches for demsef forget God, because life and wealth fit end sharp sharp. Na dis one Luke 12:16-21 teach.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector, both men went to the temple to pray, yet Jesus said the tax collector returned home justified before God rather than the Pharisee. What did the tax collector do that pleased God?
o: He humbled himself and simply asked God for mercy
He fasted twice a week like the Pharisee
He gave more money in tithes than the Pharisee
He prayed loudly in the temple so others could hear him
questions.e: Unlike the proud Pharisee who boasted of his own righteousness, the tax collector stood at a distance, beat his chest and humbly begged God for mercy, which is why Jesus said he, not the Pharisee, went home justified. This is in Luke 18:13-14.
questions.p: Unlike the proud Pharisee wey dey praise imsef, the tax collector stand far, beat im chest, and humbly beg God make E show am mercy, na im make Jesus talk say na im dey justified pass the Pharisee. Dis dey Luke 18:13-14.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins, five were described as wise and five as foolish while they waited for the bridegroom at night. What was the main difference between the wise and the foolish virgins?
o: The wise virgins slept while they waited for the bridegroom
The wise virgins took extra oil along with their lamps
The wise virgins arrived at the wedding earlier than the foolish ones
The wise virgins carried brighter lamps than the foolish ones
questions.e: Both groups fell asleep while waiting, but the wise virgins had brought extra oil in flasks for their lamps, so they were ready when the bridegroom suddenly arrived, unlike the foolish ones whose lamps ran out. This is recorded in Matthew 25:3-4.
questions.p: Both groups sleep while dem dey wait, but the wise virgins carry extra oil for their flask so dem ready when the bridegroom come sudden, but the foolish ones lamp just finish. Na so Matthew 25:3-4 talk am.

questions.q: In the Beatitudes recorded in Matthew chapter 5, Jesus said the poor in spirit are blessed because they will receive what?
questions.e: Jesus said 'Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven' (Matthew 5:3). The other rewards belong to different Beatitudes: the meek inherit the earth, mourners are comforted, and the merciful obtain mercy.
questions.p: Jesus talk say 'Blessed na the poor in spirit, because kingdom of heaven na their own' (Matthew 5:3). The other rewards dey for different Beatitudes: meek go get earth, those wey mourn go get comfort, and merciful go get mercy.

questions.q: Jesus told His disciples, 'You are the salt of the earth and the light of the world.' What lesson was He teaching them through this picture?
o: They should influence the world positively with good deeds
They should avoid eating salty food
They should build their houses on high hills
questions.e: In Matthew 5:13-16, Jesus used salt and light to show that believers should live good lives that preserve society and show others the way, just as salt preserves and light reveals. This is about godly influence, not literal food or buildings.
questions.p: For Matthew 5:13-16, Jesus use salt and light show say believers suppose live good life wey go help society and show people correct way, just like how salt dey preserve and light dey show road. E no be about food or house.

questions.q: In the Lord's Prayer taught by Jesus in Matthew chapter 6, what did He instruct believers to request from God every day?
questions.e: The Lord's Prayer includes the request 'Give us this day our daily bread' (Matthew 6:11), teaching believers to depend on God for their everyday needs.
questions.p: Inside the Lord's Prayer, Jesus teach say make believers pray 'Give us this day our daily bread' (Matthew 6:11), to show say dem suppose depend on God for everyday needs.

questions.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught that if someone slaps a believer on the right cheek, the believer should do what?
o: Slap him back twice as hard
Turn the other cheek to him also
Report the matter to the elders
questions.e: Jesus taught, 'But I tell you, do not resist an evil person. If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to them the other cheek also' (Matthew 5:39). This teaching discourages revenge and promotes patience.
questions.p: Jesus talk say make person no fight back wicked person; if somebody slap your right cheek, turn the other one give am (Matthew 5:39). Na patience and no revenge e dey teach.

questions.q: In the parable of the wise and the foolish builders, the house built on the rock represents a person who does what?
o: Prays five times daily without fail
Hears Jesus' words and puts them into practice
questions.e: Jesus explained that everyone who hears His words and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock, which stood firm during the storm (Matthew 7:24-27). The foolish builder heard but did not obey.
questions.p: Jesus explain say anybody wey hear im word and obey am na like wise man wey build house for rock, wey stand strong during storm (Matthew 7:24-27). The foolish one hear but no obey.

questions.q: When Jesus taught His disciples to 'ask, seek and knock' in Matthew chapter 7, He was encouraging them to do what?
o: Ask many questions during His teaching
Knock on neighbours' doors for help
Be persistent and sincere in prayer
questions.e: Jesus said, 'Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you' (Matthew 7:7-8). This teaching encourages believers to be persistent and confident in prayer.
questions.p: Jesus talk say 'Ask and dem go give you; seek and you go find am; knock and door go open for you' (Matthew 7:7-8). E dey teach say make believers no tire for prayer, make dem get confidence.

questions.q: Jesus warned His followers not to store up treasures on earth mainly because such treasures do what?
o: Attract unnecessary taxation from the government
Can be destroyed by moth and rust or stolen by thieves
Make a person proud before his neighbours
questions.e: Jesus said earthly treasures can be destroyed by moth and rust or stolen by thieves, but treasures in heaven are safe forever (Matthew 6:19-20). He therefore urged believers to focus on heavenly, lasting treasure.
questions.p: Jesus talk say earthly treasure fit spoil because moth and rust, or thief fit steal am, but treasure for heaven safe forever (Matthew 6:19-20). So e tell believers make dem focus on heavenly treasure wey no go spoil.

questions.q: Jesus taught about two gates and two roads in Matthew chapter 7. What lesson does this teaching give about the way to eternal life?
o: Many people find the narrow gate because it is well advertised
The wide gate is safer since many people use it
Few people find the narrow gate that leads to life because it demands discipline
Both gates eventually lead to the same destination
questions.e: Jesus said the gate to destruction is wide and many enter through it, but the gate to life is narrow and few find it (Matthew 7:13-14). The lesson is that true discipleship requires discipline and commitment, unlike the easy, popular path many follow.
questions.p: Jesus talk say the gate wey dey lead to destruction wide and plenty people dey enter am, but the gate wey dey lead to life narrow and na small people dey find am (Matthew 7:13-14). The lesson na say to follow Jesus well need discipline, e no be popular or easy road.

questions.q: Who was the Roman governor that presided over the trial of Jesus Christ before He was sentenced to death?
questions.e: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea who heard Jesus' case and later ordered His crucifixion. This is recorded in Matthew 27:2 and John 18:29.
questions.p: Pontius Pilate na di Roman governor wey hear Jesus case and later order say make dem crucify am. Dis one dey for Matthew 27:2 and John 18:29.

questions.q: During the trial of Jesus, which of His disciples denied knowing Him three times?
questions.e: Peter denied Jesus three times while Jesus was being tried, just as Jesus had earlier predicted. This is found in Luke 22:54-62.
questions.p: Peter na im deny Jesus three times while dem dey try Jesus, just as Jesus don tell am before. Dis one dey for Luke 22:54-62.

questions.q: Immediately after His arrest in the Garden of Gethsemane, before whom was Jesus first taken for questioning?
questions.e: After His arrest, Jesus was first taken to Annas before being sent to Caiaphas the high priest. This order of events is recorded in John 18:12-13.
questions.p: After dem arrest Jesus, dem first carry am go Annas before dem later send am go Caiaphas di high priest. Dis order dey John 18:12-13.

questions.q: Who was compelled by the Roman soldiers to carry the cross of Jesus to the place of crucifixion?
questions.e: Simon of Cyrene was forced by the soldiers to carry the cross when Jesus could no longer bear it. This is recorded in Matthew 27:32 and Luke 23:26.
questions.p: Simon of Cyrene na im soldiers force make e carry di cross when Jesus body no fit again. Dis one dey for Matthew 27:32 and Luke 23:26.

questions.q: What inscription did Pilate order to be written and placed above Jesus on the cross?
o: This is the Son of God
Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews
questions.e: Pilate ordered the inscription 'Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews' to be placed above Jesus on the cross, written in Hebrew, Latin and Greek. This is recorded in John 19:19.
questions.p: Pilate order say make dem write 'Jesus of Nazareth, King of di Jews' put for top di cross, dem write am for Hebrew, Latin and Greek. Dis one dey John 19:19.

questions.q: Why did Pilate wash his hands in front of the crowd during the trial of Jesus?
o: To follow Jewish purification customs before judgement
To show that he was not guilty of condemning an innocent man
To prepare himself for the Passover feast
To calm the angry crowd before releasing Barabbas
questions.e: Pilate washed his hands to publicly declare that he was innocent of Jesus' blood, even though he still handed Him over to be crucified. This act is recorded in Matthew 27:24.
questions.p: Pilate wash im hand well-well to show say im no get hand for Jesus blood, even though na im still hand Jesus over make dem crucify am. Dis one dey Matthew 27:24.

questions.q: According to the Gospel of John, who was the first person Jesus appeared to after His resurrection?
questions.e: John's Gospel records that Jesus first appeared to Mary Magdalene at the tomb after His resurrection, before He appeared to the other disciples. This is found in John 20:11-16.
questions.p: John Gospel show say Mary Magdalene na di first person wey Jesus show imself to for di tomb after e resurrect, before e later show for di oda disciples. Dis one dey John 20:11-16.

questions.q: What was the name of the place, meaning 'the place of a skull', where Jesus was crucified?
questions.e: Jesus was crucified at Golgotha, a place whose name means 'the place of a skull'. This is recorded in Mark 15:22 and John 19:17.
questions.p: Dem crucify Jesus for Golgotha, wey im name mean 'di place of skull'. Dis one dey Mark 15:22 and John 19:17.

questions.q: On the day of Pentecost, as recorded in Acts chapter 2, what visible sign appeared and rested on each of the disciples when the Holy Spirit came upon them?
questions.e: The Bible says divided tongues like fire appeared and sat on each of the disciples, and they were filled with the Holy Spirit. This is recorded in Acts 2:1-4.
questions.p: Bible talk say tongue of fire come show and sidon on top each of di disciples wen Holy Spirit full dem. Dis dey for Acts 2:1-4.

questions.q: After Peter preached his sermon on the day of Pentecost, about how many people believed and were added to the church through baptism?
questions.e: Acts 2:41 records that those who gladly received Peter's message were baptised, and about three thousand souls were added to the church that day.
questions.p: Acts 2:41 talk say people wey hear Peter sermon take am serious, dem baptise dem, and around three thousand people join di church dat day.

questions.q: When Philip went down to preach the gospel of Christ in a certain city, the people gave him great attention because of the miracles he performed, and there was great joy in that city. Which city was this?
questions.e: Acts 8:5-8 records that Philip preached Christ in Samaria, cast out unclean spirits and healed the sick, which brought great joy to the city.
questions.p: Acts 8:5-8 show say na Samaria Philip go preach Christ, e cast out bad spirit and heal sick people, and di whole city dey happy well well.

questions.q: Peter and John healed a man who had been lame from birth as they went into the temple to pray. At which gate of the temple was this man sitting to beg for alms?
questions.e: Acts 3:2 states that the lame man was laid daily at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, where he asked alms of those entering.
questions.p: Acts 3:2 talk say dem dey carry di lame man put everyday for di gate wey dem call Beautiful Gate, make e dey beg money from people wey wan enter temple.

questions.q: Stephen was dragged before the Jewish council (Sanhedrin) after false witnesses accused him of blasphemy. According to Acts chapter 6, what two things did they claim he spoke against?
o: the temple and the law of Moses
the king and the Roman army
questions.e: Acts 6:13-14 says the false witnesses claimed Stephen spoke blasphemous words against the holy temple and the law, saying Jesus would destroy the temple and change the customs of Moses.
questions.p: Acts 6:13-14 show say di false witness dem claim say Stephen talk bad against di temple and di law of Moses, say Jesus go destroy di temple and change dia custom.

questions.q: The apostles appointed seven men full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom (including Stephen and Philip) to serve tables after a complaint arose in the early church. Who were complaining of being neglected in the daily distribution of food?
questions.e: Acts 6:1 records that the Grecian Jews complained against the Hebrews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food, leading to the appointment of seven men to handle the task fairly.
questions.p: Acts 6:1 talk say na di Grecian widows dey complain say dem no dey share food give dem well, dat na why dem choose seven men wey get Holy Spirit to handle di matter.

questions.q: On his way from Jerusalem, an Ethiopian official in charge of the treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, was reading from an Old Testament book when Philip met him and explained the scripture to him. Which book was he reading?
questions.e: Acts 8:27-35 records that the Ethiopian eunuch was reading from the prophet Isaiah, specifically about the suffering servant, and Philip used this passage to preach Jesus to him.
questions.p: Acts 8:27-35 show say di Ethiopian official dey read from book of Isaiah, di part wey talk about suffering servant, and Philip use am take preach Jesus give am.

questions.q: Before Pentecost, the disciples were hiding behind locked doors for fear of the Jewish leaders. After receiving the Holy Spirit, Peter stood boldly before a large crowd and openly preached about Jesus Christ. What important lesson about the Holy Spirit does this change in Peter's behaviour teach?
o: The Holy Spirit makes believers no longer need to pray
The Holy Spirit works only through church leaders
The Holy Spirit removes all future suffering from believers
The Holy Spirit gives believers power and boldness to witness for Christ
questions.e: The contrast between the fearful disciples before Pentecost and the bold preaching of Peter afterward (Acts 2:14-41) shows that the Holy Spirit empowers believers with courage and boldness to witness, as Jesus had earlier promised in Acts 1:8.
questions.p: Before Pentecost, di disciples dey hide for fear, but after Holy Spirit come, Peter come dey bold preach for public (Acts 2:14-41). Dis show say Holy Spirit dey give believers power and mind to testify about Jesus, just as Jesus promise for Acts 1:8.

questions.q: What was the name of Paul before his dramatic conversion to Christianity?
questions.e: Before his conversion, Paul was known as Saul of Tarsus, a persecutor of the church. After he met Jesus, he became known as Paul. This is recorded in Acts 13:9.
questions.p: Before Paul convert, dem dey call am Saul of Tarsus, and he be person wey dey persecute church. After he meet Jesus, dem start to call am Paul. E dey for Acts 13:9.

questions.q: On which road did Paul encounter the risen Christ, an event that led to his conversion?
questions.e: Saul was travelling to Damascus to arrest Christians when a bright light from heaven shone on him and Jesus spoke to him. This encounter is recorded in Acts 9:3-4.
questions.p: Saul dey waka go Damascus to arrest Christians when bright light from heaven shine for am and Jesus talk to am. Dis story dey for Acts 9:3-4.

questions.q: Who was sent by God to visit Saul in Damascus, restore his sight, and baptize him?
questions.e: God spoke to a disciple named Ananias in a vision and sent him to lay hands on Saul so he could receive his sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit. He then baptized Saul. This is in Acts 9:17-18.
questions.p: God talk to one disciple wey dem call Ananias for vision and send am go lay hand for Saul so he go see again and receive Holy Spirit. Na him baptize Saul. Dis one dey for Acts 9:17-18.

questions.q: Who accompanied Paul on his first missionary journey as recorded in the book of Acts?
questions.e: The Holy Spirit set apart Barnabas and Saul (Paul) for missionary work, and John Mark joined them as their helper. This journey is described in Acts 13:2-5.
questions.p: Holy Spirit set Barnabas and Saul (Paul) apart for missionary work, and John Mark join dem as helper. Dis journey dey for Acts 13:2-5.

questions.q: In which city were the followers of Christ first called 'Christians'?
questions.e: After Barnabas and Saul taught many people in the city, the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch. This fact is stated in Acts 11:26.
questions.p: After Barnabas and Saul teach plenty people for dat city, na for Antioch dem first call the disciples 'Christians'. Dis one dey for Acts 11:26.

questions.q: Paul's letter to the Philippians, often described as full of joy despite hardship, was written while he was:
o: teaching in the school of Tyrannus
staying in Corinth with Priscilla and Aquila
questions.e: Paul wrote to the Philippians while he was a prisoner, yet he encouraged them to rejoice always, showing his faith despite his chains. This background is reflected in Philippians 1:12-13.
questions.p: Paul write to Philippi church as prisoner, but he still tell dem make dem dey rejoice always, dis one show say he still get strong faith even for chain. Dis background dey for Philippians 1:12-13.

questions.q: On his way to Rome as a prisoner, Paul's ship was wrecked near which island, where he later healed the sick?
questions.e: During a storm, the ship carrying Paul to Rome wrecked, and all on board safely reached the island of Malta, where Paul healed many people, including the father of the chief official. This is recorded in Acts 28:1.
questions.p: During heavy storm, the ship wey dey carry Paul go Rome wreck, but everybody land well for Malta island, and Paul heal plenty people dia, including the chief official papa. Dis one dey for Acts 28:1.

questions.q: Paul's letter to the Galatians was mainly written to correct believers who were being misled to think that:
o: the second coming of Christ had already taken place
spiritual gifts were no longer needed in the church
gentile believers must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses to be saved
Christ had not truly risen from the dead
questions.e: False teachers had convinced some Galatian believers that they needed circumcision and obedience to the Mosaic law in addition to faith in Christ for salvation. Paul firmly corrected this error, teaching that salvation is by faith alone. This teaching is found in Galatians 2:16 and 5:1-4.
questions.p: Some false teachers don confuse some Galatia believers say dem need circumcision and must obey Moses law before dem fit save, no be only faith for Christ. Paul correct dis mistake, e teach say na only faith fit save person. Dis teaching dey for Galatians 2:16 and 5:1-4.

questions.q: According to James 2:26, faith without works is like what?
o: A dead body without the spirit
questions.e: James 2:26 says 'faith without works is dead, as the body without the spirit is dead also.' This teaches that true faith must show itself through good deeds.
questions.p: James 2:26 talk say faith wey no get work na like body wey no get spirit, e don die. Dis one dey teach say real faith must show for action.

questions.q: In Romans 13:1, Christians are told to submit to governing authorities mainly because
o: there is no power except from God
civil laws are greater than God's law
questions.e: Romans 13:1 states that there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist have been established by Him. This is why believers are told to submit to them as part of civic duty.
questions.p: Romans 13:1 talk say no power dey wey no come from God, na God put all authorities for their position. Na why believer go dey submit to dem as part of im civic duty.

questions.q: According to 1 Peter 4:8, what does love do?
o: It guarantees long life for believers
It covers a multitude of sins
It replaces the need for faith
It removes every form of suffering
questions.e: 1 Peter 4:8 says to have fervent love among yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins. This teaches that genuine love helps believers overlook and forgive one another's faults.
questions.p: 1 Peter 4:8 talk say make una get strong love for una midst because love dey cover plenty sin. E mean say if you get real love, you go fit forgive person im wrongdoing.

questions.q: In James 2:21, Abraham was said to be justified by works when he did what?
o: Built an altar and called on God's name
Left Haran for an unknown land
Offered his son Isaac on the altar
questions.e: James 2:21 says Abraham was justified by works when he offered his son Isaac on the altar, showing that his faith was proved real by his obedient action.
questions.p: James 2:21 talk say Abraham get justification through work when e carry im son Isaac go altar. Na dat action show say im faith na real one.

questions.q: According to Romans 12:2, instead of being conformed to this world, believers should be
o: transformed by the renewing of their mind
justified by keeping the Mosaic law
baptized repeatedly in the Holy Spirit
questions.e: Romans 12:2 instructs believers not to be conformed to the pattern of this world but to be transformed by the renewing of their mind, so they can discern God's good and acceptable will.
questions.p: Romans 12:2 talk say make believer no follow dis world pattern, make dem change through di renewing of dia mind. Na dat way dem go fit know God im good and perfect will.

questions.q: In James chapter 2, which Old Testament woman was justified by works for hiding the messengers and sending them out another way?
questions.e: James 2:25 gives Rahab the harlot as an example of justification by works because she hid the spies sent to Jericho and helped them escape safely.
questions.p: James 2:25 give Rahab di harlot as example of work wey show real faith, because she hide di spies wey dem send go Jericho and help dem run comot safe.

questions.q: According to 1 Peter 2:20, which type of suffering brings no credit before God?
questions.e: 1 Peter 2:20 explains that there is no credit in patiently enduring punishment for doing wrong; it is suffering for doing good that is commendable before God. The verse contrasts the two kinds of suffering to show which pleases God.
questions.p: 1 Peter 2:20 explain say no credit dey if you suffer because you do bad thing; na when you suffer for doing good e dey pleasing to God. Di verse dey compare di two kain suffer to show which one God dey happy with.

questions.q: A student argues that James' teaching that 'faith without works is dead' contradicts Paul's teaching in Romans that a person is justified by faith. Which statement best resolves this apparent conflict?
o: James and Paul both agree that genuine, living faith naturally produces good works
James rejects Paul's teaching on salvation by grace completely
Paul teaches that works alone, without faith, can save a person
James teaches that keeping the Mosaic law alone brings salvation
questions.e: Paul (Romans) stresses that salvation begins with faith, while James stresses that real faith must show itself in works; both agree genuine faith is never alone but produces a changed, obedient life. The two teachings complement rather than contradict each other.
questions.p: Paul (for Romans) dey talk say salvation dey start with faith, while James dey talk say real faith go show itself through work; both of dem agree say true faith no fit stay alone, e go produce change and obedience. So di two teaching dey match, dem no dey contradict each other.
